claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, let me start with a basic question:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child. I'm inquiring about my daughter Alex - she's 3 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one daughter, Alex, who is 3 years old.

Now I need to ask you some questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit would provide (or equivalent support) towards her care - such as for food, clothes, or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check one more important aspect:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually there is a bit of a situation there. Alex's other parent and I are both responsible for her, and we haven't been able to agree on who should claim the Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that situation. That's helpful to know.

Just to clarify: **Has either you or Alex's other parent already submitted a claim for Child Benefit for Alex, or are you both planning to claim but haven't submitted applications yet?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We haven't submitted any applications yet - we're both trying to figure out who should claim it, but we can't agree on who that should be.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation paid for by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not in hospital or in care or anything like that. She's just at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Are there any circumstances where Alex lives with someone else (other than you and her other parent), or is she in your care full-time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's with me full-time. She lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question to complete my assessment:

**Do you have the right to reside in the UK? For example, are you a UK citizen, do you have settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or any other immigration status that gives you the right to reside here?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and have the right to reside here.

## Assessment Complete

Based on the information you've provided, **you are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Summary for Alex (age 3):
You meet all the eligibility criteria:
- Alex is under 16 years old
- You live in the UK and have the right to reside here
- You live with Alex and are responsible for her care
- Alex is not in hospital or care
- No one is currently claiming Child Benefit for her

### Important Information About Your Situation:

Regarding the disagreement with Alex's other parent about who should claim: The rules state that only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. You and Alex's other parent should try to agree between yourselves who will claim. However, **you are eligible to submit a claim**. 

If both you and the other parent submit separate claims for Alex, HMRC will make the decision about who will receive the Child Benefit.

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit for Alex if you wish to do so.
